chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me who said: Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd narrated to me, from Zakariyya al-Mu'min, from Muhammad ibn Rabah al-Qalla, who said:

I saw Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) having phlebotomy done on Friday. I said: May I be your ransom, do you have phlebotomy done on Friday? He said: I recite the Verse of the Throne. So whenever blood rises in you, whether by night or by day, recite the Verse of the Throne and have phlebotomy done.

key_terms.أَبَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Abu Ibrahim (title of Imam al-Kadhim, peace be upon him)
key_terms.هَاجَ الدَّمُ: Blood rose/accumulated (referring to high blood pressure or congestion)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on having phlebotomy done on Friday according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith highlights the Prophetic tradition of cupping on Fridays, emphasizing the spiritual potency of Ayat al-Kursi as a protective measure against bodily impurities or 'rising blood.' It reflects the Shia emphasis on integrating physical hygiene with divine remembrance, where the recitation serves as a spiritual safeguard during the ritual. This practice underscores the holistic view of health in Shia jurisprudence, linking temporal actions with eternal spiritual benefits.
